title: Six people force a trio of mutual acquaintances or strangers
body: Suppose each pair in a group of six has either met or never met. Pick one person. At least three others have the same relationship to them. Either two of those three form a matching trio with that person, or the three themselves form the opposite kind of trio.
takeaway: A large enough group forces a pattern even when nobody planned the relationships.
source: Wolfram MathWorld, Ramsey Number and Ramsey Graph
visual: six small nodes connected by threads of two colours

title: Four dice can each be favoured against one of the others
body: Bradley Efron's four dice have different sets of numbers on their faces. The first beats the second two-thirds of the time, and the same odds apply from the second to the third, the third to the fourth and the fourth back to the first.
takeaway: The best die to choose depends on the one your opponent chooses.
visual: four different-coloured dice arranged in a loose circle
